brief.deck: TensorWave, the Las Vegas-based all-AMD GPU cloud, announced on 10 June 2026 a $350M Series B at a $1.55B valuation co-led by Magnetar and AMD Ventures, almost four times the price of its $100M Series A thirteen months earlier, with an 8,192-GPU cluster live and 2 GW of capacity secured.
brief.the_case_p1: On 10 June TensorWave announced a $350M Series B at a $1.55B valuation, co-led by Magnetar and AMD Ventures with Maverick Silicon, Nexus Venture Partners and Western Frontier; the same leads backed the $100M Series A of May 2025 at a reported $400M. The capital funds AMD Instinct MI355X clusters on top of an 8,192-GPU MI325X training cluster already live and more than 2 GW of data-centre capacity secured. Revenue is reported only: the 2025 release projected a run rate above $100M by year-end. Founded in Las Vegas in 2023, it is AMD's flagship challenger in the cloud.
brief.the_case_p2: The grid has priced this archetype: CoreWeave became Aston Martin Aramco's Official AI Cloud Computing Partner in May 2025 and Core Scientific sits with Cadillac. Both run Nvidia silicon; TensorWave is the AMD alternative, and AMD, its co-lead investor, is already a partner of Mercedes. A neocloud that has just quadrupled its price needs enterprise buyers, not only AI labs, and a home race in Las Vegas in November.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The round closed on 10 June; brand budgets reset in the quarter after a raise. The United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November), TensorWave's home city, are the US rounds left in 2026, and teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter.
brief.why_team_para: Haas is the grid's American privateer, headquartered in Kannapolis, North Carolina; Toyota Gazoo Racing is title partner from 2026, with Mphasis, Ruckus and CommScope on the technology side. No cloud, GPU or AI-compute partner sits on the car, so Official AI Compute Partner is a clean category at a price a first-time sponsor can defend. Three US races give a Las Vegas company a home round, and the leanest team gains most from compute delivered in kind. Every other large team carries an incumbent.
brief.value_section_label: VALUE TO TGR HAAS F1 TEAM
brief.value_content: MODE A - operational. The work outside the FIA aero-testing limits is compute-hungry: machine-learning surrogates, driver-in-the-loop and strategy simulation, telemetry and video analytics between sessions. TensorWave supplies elastic AMD Instinct GPU capacity on demand, part of it in kind, so the leanest team on the cost cap buys capability without capital. In return: Official AI Compute Partner status, livery presence, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official AI Compute Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, spanning the MI355X build-out. Estimated $2-4M a year, part-payable in compute credits. Scope: sidepod placement, naming of the team's compute environment, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality, engineering content.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Horton co-founded TensorWave in Las Vegas in 2023 and fronts every raise; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Piotr Tomasik, Co-Founder, President and COO, and Jeff Tatarchuk, Co-Founder and Chief Growth Officer. No CMO or CFO is listed.
brief.opening_angle_intro: Lead with the Las Vegas home race.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Darrick, CoreWeave took its seat at Aston Martin the year it listed; the AMD story has no seat, and the American team's compute lane is open. Las Vegas is your home race. 25 minutes before Austin to see the numbers in kind?”
score_cells: Round closed 10 Jun; Austin and Las Vegas inside the window.
$450M raised in total at $1.55B; revenue reported as a projection only.
B2B infrastructure; Las Vegas home story; challenger narrative.
No hard deadline beyond Q4 rosters and the Las Vegas GP.
MODE A: elastic GPU capacity outside the aero cap, part in kind.
risks: At $1.55B TensorWave is a fraction of CoreWeave's size and its revenue is a reported 2025 projection; a cash fee competes with GPU purchases.
Structure most of the value in compute credits; keep the cash component inside a first-timer's budget.
AMD, the co-lead investor, is a Mercedes partner; a rival team may read a TensorWave deal as AMD-adjacent.
Position it as the neocloud lane, not the silicon lane; keep AMD branding out of the Haas activation.
brief.bottom_line: A $350M round at $1.55B on 10 June, a live 8,192-GPU cluster and 2 GW of secured capacity put TensorWave at peak brand-investment authority; the compute lane at the American team is open and its home race in Las Vegas sits inside the window.

why_now.label: Trigger
why_now.text: On 10 June 2026 TensorWave announced a $350M Series B at a $1.55B valuation, co-led by Magnetar and AMD Ventures with Maverick Silicon, Nexus Venture Partners and Western Frontier. The release is the company's own on Business Wire, so the round and valuation are VERIFIED; the revenue figure is not, and the brief says so.

why_now.label: Price quadrupled in thirteen months
why_now.text: The $100M Series A of May 2025 valued the company at a reported $400M; the Series B is almost four times that. A company re-priced this fast has a story to tell to enterprise buyers, bankers and the public markets, and a budget to tell it with.

why_now.label: Capacity is real
why_now.text: An 8,192-GPU AMD Instinct MI325X training cluster is live, more than 2 GW of long-term data-centre capacity is secured, and the new capital funds MI355X clusters. Each cluster that goes live is a milestone the partnership can be timed to.

why_now.label: Calendar window
why_now.text: The United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two US rounds left in 2026; Las Vegas is TensorWave's home city. Teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter, so a deal agreed before Austin can be announced at home and activated in full for 2027.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: Haas carries Toyota Gazoo Racing as title partner with Mphasis (services), Ruckus (networking), CommScope and Haas Automation on the technology side. No cloud, GPU or AI-compute partner: Official AI Compute Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.

why_team.label: The American team for a Las Vegas company
why_team.text: Haas is headquartered in Kannapolis, North Carolina, and races three US rounds (Miami, Austin, Las Vegas). For a Las Vegas company selling to US enterprises, the Las Vegas GP is a home race on the only American team.

why_team.label: Where compute in kind counts most
why_team.text: The leanest team on the cost cap is the one where elastic GPU capacity delivered as part of the fee changes what the engineering team can do. That makes Haas a reference customer, not a logo, which is what TensorWave's enterprise sellers need.

why_team.label: The incumbents elsewhere
why_team.text: CoreWeave at Aston Martin, Core Scientific at Cadillac, Google Cloud and Dell at McLaren, Oracle at Red Bull, Microsoft at Mercedes and Alpine, HP and IBM at Ferrari: every other large team carries a cloud or compute partner. Williams and Audi are open but offer no US or Las Vegas thread.

value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)
value.text: Compute for the work outside the aerodynamic-testing restrictions: machine-learning surrogates, driver-in-the-loop and race-strategy simulation, telemetry and video analytics between sessions. TensorWave supplies AMD Instinct GPU capacity on demand, part of it as credits inside the fee, so the team buys capability without capital.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: A partner that sells to CIOs, AI labs and enterprises brings a guest list of technology buyers, investors and bankers to Austin and Las Vegas, the audience Haas's other B2B partners want in the suite.

value.label: Content and ecosystem
value.text: A data-centre-to-pit-wall story the team can tell on camera; a documented factory reference customer for TensorWave's enterprise sales; and a bridge into AMD's ecosystem of software and silicon partners.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official AI Compute Partner designation, engine-cover or sidepod placement, naming of the team's compute environment, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality, driver and engineering access for TensorWave's channels.

ruled_out.reason: CoreWeave, Official AI Cloud Computing Partner since May 2025, is a direct rival.
Core Scientific (datacentre and HPC hosting) and TWG AI occupy the compute and AI lanes.

ruled_out.team: Oracle Red Bull Racing · Visa Cash App Racing Bulls
ruled_out.reason: Oracle is the Red Bull group's cloud incumbent and title partner of the senior team.
Microsoft and Hewlett Packard Enterprise hold cloud and compute; AMD itself is a partner.

ruled_out.team: McLaren Mastercard F1 Team · BWT Alpine
ruled_out.reason: Google Cloud and Dell at McLaren; Microsoft at Alpine.
HP (title) and IBM cover compute hardware and cloud services.

ruled_out.team: Atlassian Williams Racing · Audi F1 Team
ruled_out.reason: Open but not chosen: no US or Las Vegas thread; Audi carried HPE within the last 12 months.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Darrick Horton before the United States GP to size an Official AI Compute Partner entry at Haas, part-paid in compute credits, with a Las Vegas GP announcement window and full activation from 2027.

The row's trigger holds and is dated to the row: **$350M Series B at a $1.55B valuation, co-led by Magnetar and AMD Ventures, Business Wire release of 10 Jun 2026** (URL stamp 20260610). The row carried no team. AMD is a Mercedes partner; that is named as a risk, not hidden. Case N° 193 (UiPath) in this batch also recommends Haas: our signals are not placements, and each is judged against the real roster only. Two 2026 Haas additions sit outside the sponsor table and are not written as "Brand at Team" in the copy: Emburse (travel and expense, 3 Jun 2026) and Exein (physical AI security); neither is a compute rival.
